title: The Market Collapse Shock
speaker: Kevin Paffrath (Meet Kevin)

macro_themes.view: TS Lombard data show record Japanese selling of US Treasuries; a BoJ hike while the Fed holds widens the spread and could worsen it before it gets better.
Challenger layoffs down, PMI/ISM strong, lending standards loose and GPU rental prices rising: the AI boom is mid-cycle, not rolling over.
Breadth and equal-weight S&P at extreme fear and financials breaking down while a few tech names carry the Nasdaq.
90-95% confident of an Iran deal by the election; once that and Japanese selling end, bond yields fall and stocks rocket.

calls.condition: Needs an Iran deal and an end to Japanese Treasury selling; volatility possible for ~3 weeks
calls.reason: Bought the dip heavily at 700-715; once Japanese repatriation and the Iran war end, yields drop and stocks go to the moon; expects record highs and QQQ above 800 by year-end.
calls.quote: we'll probably exceed 800 on the NASDAQ 100 by the end of the year

calls.reason: Called 5.27% as near the peak (it reached 5.32); Japanese selling may persist short term, but an Iran deal brings yields down.
calls.quote: 5.27 is when I called the 10-year Treasury as we are pretty damn close to peak

calls.reason: Oil pricing pressure has slowed after peaking at 107-109 in early September, declining back toward $100, and should go lower on an Iran deal.
calls.quote: We've got oil declining back to $100. And honestly, it's probably once we get an Iran deal, it's going to go even lower

notes: "Happy October" with Challenger and ISM reports this morning => Thu Oct 1 (listing Oct 2). "Nasdaq 100 exceed 800" interpreted in QQQ units (consistent with his 735/715 QQQ levels).
